turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first, so start there.
"Upset." Don't manage me, Hale. Who decided on that zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
But I'm not changing the grade.
"Not changing the grade." Then tell me the basis, because your own procedure says the parent is called before any mark goes in, and nobody called me. I'm writing that down.
I'm still not changing it. Keep going if you like.

Then I'll stop asking you and ask the principal, today, after my call. You've given me no basis, no document, and no reason a 17-year-old learned his mark from a phone. If you have something to show me, this is the minute to do it.
You can say it ten more ways. The answer is no.
Fine, then answer something else. Is anything about this on Owen's record right now, yes or no? Because if you won't move the mark, I want that in writing before I walk upstairs.
